page0.text:
Two dark figures clash.
One of them is Rider, who dashes at supersonic speed, unleashing a dizzying flurry of attacks from the ground, the air, front and back, left and right.
The way her long hair trails behind her as she streaks back and forth resembles a shooting star.

page1.text:
And yet...
The shooting star is all too feeble.
Rider's target is the swordswoman.
Saber takes a firm, assured stance and intercepts Rider's assault with overwhelming force. It fails to budge her at all.

page2.text:
Rider leaps and strikes from unexpected and wild angles, but Saber just needs to turn and bat her daggers aside. Her ripostes steadily break Rider down.
Her firmness and fierceness are like that of a black sun.
A giant star that burns any who approach it.
Even if it can fly through the air, a shooting star that could blink out at any second could never overcome a sun.

page3.text:
"Hah...argh..."
Another of Rider's ambushes fails, and her strength is shaved away.
She boasts superhuman speed, but she's being forced back by Saber's counterattacks.
In the blink of an eye, she retreats and charges like a dark firework.
But she's only barely evading mortal injury.

page4.text:
The difference in strength is clear.
Rider's speed drops with each assault.
High-speed movement and rapid attacks too fast for the eye to follow.
Any of Saber's injuries are automatically healed.
The conclusion seems forgone.
It takes every last drop of Rider's energy to suppress Saber.

page5.text:
Rider keeps attacking, while Saber stops her with attacks of her own.
Rider knows that she and the boy she calls Master will be killed instantly if Saber goes on the offense.
So she keeps running, knowing that she's going to burn out soon.

page6.text:
Her strength is sapped with each passing second.
Rider said that she could hold out for two minutes.
It has already been ten minutes since she passed that point.
Her legs are starting to collapse from within under the extreme strain.

page7.text:
Meanwhile, Saber is completely unharmed.
All of Rider's attacks have failed to reach Saber, while Saber remains firmly planted, showing no sign of fatigue.
Skill. Strength. Magical energy.
Saber has the overwhelming advantage in all three.
So, the instant Rider loses her only edge, her speed, Saber will most likely move.
Rider's mobility steadily declines.
...It's only a matter of time before Saber catches her.
She'll be forced to catch her breath after a few more seconds, probably once the next attack is repelled.
Once Rider loses her physical and magical strength and can't operate at full output anymore, Saber will cut her in two.

page8.text:
...
But they predicted this situation.
Before setting out for the cave, Rider and the boy both knew
that the battle would run this way.
She knows that this is a losing tactic.

page9.text:
There is only one way to avert her death.
They wait for the opportunity with bated breath.
Rider attacks Saber.
At the same time,
I loosen the binding on my left arm,
and I
begin
Projecting.

page10.text:
I'm fading away.
I loosen the holy shroud around Archer's left arm.

page11.text:
Search.
I'm being blown away.
The wind is powerful.
I'm beginning to fail to understand anything I see, making me want to cry.

page12.text:
Release my right hand.
Put the shroud back on.
I can't take this for even a second.
I'll lose it.
I'll lose what's precious to me.
SearchSelect.
No, in this moment, every part of my body is dead.

page13.text:
Rider is fighting for her life.
She isn't whining.
I     I too    need to do what I can, I can figh—
I can't lose focus for even a second.
Rider will decide the timing.
I need to free my left arm in advance, so I can be ready

page15.text:
But it hurts.
It hurts. I'm scared.
Hurry—hurry, are—yet, Ri—?

page16.text:
...
I disappear.
I just lost something important.
I can't remember what I lost.
I just know that there was something I kept close, and I'll never remember it again.

page18.text:
Something rips.
My right lung is torn out from inside.

page19.text:
"Guh...fgh."
Still not yet?
My mind won't last.
Rider's desperate, too.
We won't lose.
Look directly at Rider, with your heart and soul.
She left her life in your hands.
Rider has her battle to fight.
And I'll fight my way—

page20.text:
"...!"
Rider stops moving.
She's on her knees in front of Saber. Maybe she's too weak to retreat.
